From: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Argus MSA - redline (consequential damages)

Lauren — quick thoughts below; happy to jump on a call with you and Argus counsel.

Summary position: prefer mutual exclusion with tightly-drawn exceptions. Rationale: across sales we’ve moved to mutual clauses to avoid asymmetry fights and prevent counterparty leverage in renewals. We should, however, be firm that "lost profits" are only recoverable where directly caused by Redwood’s gross negligence or willful misconduct and in respect of a narrow set of operational failures (e.g., data destruction due to misconfiguration of a Dedicated instance).

Proposed drafting approach (high level):
- Keep phraseology: "Neither party shall be liable to the other for indirect, special, incidental, consequential, exemplary or punitive damages, including loss of profits, revenue, business opportunity or data, except as set forth below."
- Carve-outs (non-exhaustive):
  • Liability arising from each party’s indemnification obligations for third-party IP infringement;
  • Liability for a party’s gross negligence or willful misconduct;
  • Liability for breach of confidentiality or unauthorized data access that results in regulatory fines;
  • Liability for direct remediation costs to restore or reasonably attempt to restore customer data.
- Lost profits cap: where lost profits are recoverable under the gross negligence/willful misconduct carve-out, cap recovery at the greater of (a) fees paid under the applicable Order Form in the prior 12 months or (b) $2,500,000 — this provides predictability while acknowledging higher-risk situations.

We should avoid language that leaves "consequential" undefined. Suggest adding a sentence: "For clarity, 'consequential damages' do not include direct damages consisting of actual, documented costs reasonably incurred to remediate a data loss event."

I’ll prepare tracked-language for Lauren to send to Argus if you’re comfortable with that cap figure.

-Rafael
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Liu <tom.liu@argusbio.com>

Lauren — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple points from our side:
- Argus’ outside counsel insists on mutuality because their procurement team wants reciprocal protections in the event Argus provides data or tooling that causes downstream issues.
- On lost profits carve-out: they are open to a gross-negligence threshold but want the cap to be a multiple of 12 months' fees (they suggested 3x ARR) because our services are core to several of their revenue-generating assays.
- They asked whether Redwood will agree to express language that "consequential damages include, but are not limited to, loss of profits and business interruption" — we want to avoid expansive enumerations.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept mutual exclusion with a gross-negligence-only lost-profits exception and whether the cap can be negotiable (i.e., 1x vs 3x ARR)?

Tom

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@argusbio.com>, Jane Foster <jane.foster@argusbio.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Argus MSA - redline (consequential damages)

Tom / Jane / Lauren — copying in with our recommended compromise and negotiation strategy. Rafael's outline informed this. Below is tracked language we recommend sending back to Argus counsel as a starting point.

Negotiation priorities:
1) Mutual exclusion is acceptable provided carve-outs are narrowly defined and the lost-profits exception is limited to gross negligence or willful misconduct.
2) Cap range: propose 1x trailing 12 months' fees as Redwood's baseline; allow 3x as an upsell / executive-approved term for strategic deals. Keep the floor at 1x to limit exposure.
3) Define consequential damages by example but exclude direct remediation costs explicitly.

Draft compromise clause (proposed):
"Neither party shall be liable to the other for indirect, special, incidental, consequential, exemplary or punitive damages, including loss of profits, revenue, business interruption or loss of data, except to the extent arising from: (a) a party’s gross negligence or willful misconduct; (b) a party’s indemnification obligations for third-party intellectual property claims; (c) breach of confidentiality obligations that results in regulatory liability; or (d) direct costs reasonably incurred to restore lost or corrupted Customer Data. Where lost profits are recoverable pursuant to clause (a), recovery shall be capped at the greater of (i) fees paid under the applicable Order Form during the 12 months preceding the event, or (ii) USD 2,500,000. The parties acknowledge that incidental or consequential damages do not include direct remediation costs expressly set out in clause (d)."

We recommend presenting the 1x vs 3x cap as a commercial lever (i.e., 1x is standard; larger cap available with commitment or executive approval). Also propose adding a short definition: "For clarity, 'consequential damages' means damages that do not flow directly from the event giving rise to liability but are derivative in nature; it does not include direct remediation costs described above."

If Argus push back on the specific dollar figure, suggest negotiating to a formula (1x fees or $2.5M floor). We should also be ready to show risk mitigation: Business continuity addendum (backup schedule), SLA credits, and runbook commitments to reduce the likelihood/severity of an incident.

-Monica
Senior Legal Counsel
Redwood Inference
